rationale: Evidence from iteration 9 (score 691.2, best so far). The oval (20/20 finishes, max_error 0.012) and s-bend (20/20, max_error 0.022) are both reliable. The slalom still finishes 0/20, but progress rose from 0.36 to 0.49 when kd went from 0.8 to 1.0. Line-loss events on the slalom rose from 1.8 to 2.25, and steering_oscillation on the s-bend rose slightly (0.36 to 0.37). The oval was essentially unchanged. The kd trend is therefore the only lever that has moved the slalom forward without hurting the two tracks that already finish. Geometry, base_speed, kp, ki and line_loss are held at iteration 9 values, so the response to kd can be attributed. Change: kd 1.0 to 1.2, a single-variable step. Expected result: slalom progress about 0.55 to 0.65, with line losses possibly still near 2 and no finish guaranteed. Oval and s-bend should hold near 1.0 completion. Hypotheses: (a) the slalom limit is loop damping at sharp bend entry, so more kd keeps raising progress; (b) if oval steering_oscillation rises above about 0.3 or oval completion drops below 0.9, derivative noise is now the limit and kd should return to about 1.0 or 1.1; (c) if slalom progress stays below 0.55, the limit is kp or sensor span, and the next test should be kp alone. Measurements wanted: completion, progress, completion_time, max_error, rms_error, line_loss_events and steering_oscillation on each track, plus control_effort for steering load.
